call.fact: Sales volume fell (131,844 t vs 140,090 t) while revenue rose: raw material costs went up after the West Asia crisis and were passed on, plus a richer mix. Management expects growth from both volume and value from next quarter.

Forex loss of Rs 25.2 cr (Rs 38.1 cr in Q4FY26) from hedges taken during rupee volatility; management says no further forex hit after Q1. Standing policy: keep positions open as imports and exports are roughly matched.

Other income comes from fixed deposits funded partly by bank borrowings and commercial paper (an interest spread), mutual funds, and mark-to-market gains on investments in IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres NCDs; it will vary 30-40% quarter to quarter.
Others EBIT fell from Rs 25 cr in Q4FY26 to Rs 1 cr: no mining in Q1 (environmental clearance awaited, 3-6 months). Revenue held up because Birla Tyres sales rose (Rs 127 cr in the quarter).
Rs 1,100 cr+ PAT in FY28 reaffirmed (double FY25's Rs 555 cr); no quarterly or annual guidance otherwise.

Announced capex ~Rs 2,000 cr: Rs 1,125 cr LFP Phase 1, Rs 368 cr announced on 15-Jul (CNT Rs 70 cr, SSCB Rs 170 cr, plus speciality chemicals), ~Rs 500 cr in Birla Tyres. About Rs 1,000 cr in FY27 and Rs 1,000 cr in FY28; self-funded, no incremental debt; no capex in coal tar distillation.

Target Rs 3,000 cr revenue in 4-5 years; EBITDA break-even expected in FY27; 49 distributors (40 domestic, 9 global), 1,000+ dealers; TBB capacity being converted to OTR over 3 years; PCR plant by FY28.

Himadri prices LFP at par with China and says its raw-material sourcing and Indian base give it a cost edge; an analyst (Anand Rathi) said its own workings showed a negative gross spread at Chinese prices. Management declined to disclose sources or margins.
R&D spend Rs 125 cr+ last year (2.6% of revenue); similar this year. FY26 R&D cited as Rs 120 cr on the Q4 call.

newEnergy.fact: Strategic investment (May-2025) plus an exclusive licence to make and sell Sicona's silicon-carbon (SiCx) anode material in India for the world. Sicona secured up to AUD 45 mn of ARENA funding; 39 OEMs/cell makers under NDA, 14 qualification programmes. Himadri holds Class A preference shares and compulsorily convertible notes (FY26 annual report, note on investments).

16.24% acquired May-2025, raised to 19.44%; nominee director. 50 MWh cell plant in South Korea since 2023; India 7 GWh gigafactory via an asset-light partner model targeted for Q4FY27. Himadri holds 27 lakh IBC shares (Rs 77.4 cr at fair value, Mar-26) plus Series A preferred stock.
40% stake with control (consolidated); electrode-material R&D and patents.

tyres.structure: Himadri, with resolution applicant Dalmia Bharat Refractories (DBRL), acquired Birla Tyres under an insolvency resolution plan (NCLT order 19-Oct-2023). The tyre undertaking sits in DBRL; Himadri holds DBRL NCDs and 8% redeemable preference shares (the purchase consideration) and owns 100% of Birla Tyres Ltd (brand company, from Apr-2025 by OCD conversion) and 49% (with control) of Himadri Birla Tyre Manufacturer, through which tyres are sold. Commercial operations restarted 29-May-2025.
tyres.scheme: On 21-Sep-2026 the board approved a scheme to demerge DBRL's tyre business into HSCL (appointed date 1-Oct-2026): 1 HSCL share for every 260 DBRL shares, about 1.76 lakh new shares (0.03% dilution). The tyre business turnover was Rs 149.31 cr in FY26. Needs exchange, SEBI, NCLT and shareholder approvals.

history.event: Incorporated in West Bengal (CIN 1987); first coal tar distillation plant in Howrah (1990); renamed Himadri Chemicals & Industries (1991); public limited company (1992). Promoters: the Choudhary family (founder Shyam Sundar Choudhary).

Built the Mahistikry (Hooghly) complex: coal tar distillation (2004), by-product refining (2006), carbon black with a captive power plant (2009); Korba plant (2007); SNF construction chemicals via a Vapi acquisition (2009).

Bain Capital's first Indian deal: Rs 412.72 cr for a minority stake (about 15% before an open offer). Bain sold down from Feb-2021 (1.19% at Rs 52.75 in Jul-2021, leaving 10.31%) and had fully exited in FY2021-22; its special rights in the articles were removed in 2025.

Carbon black expansion, Falta SEZ export unit, coal tar pitch plant in Longkou (China); coal tar distillation capacity up 60% (2014); entry into speciality carbon black (2014); Sambalpur pitch-melting plant started (2015).
Renamed Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd; continuous furnace for advanced carbon materials at Falta SEZ.
Profit trough: EBITDA margin fell to 8% (FY21) and 6% (FY22) as raw-material costs rose faster than prices; net profit Rs 47 cr and Rs 39 cr.
60,000 tpa speciality carbon black line; 60+ speciality grades; LFP cathode pilot plant. Dec-2023: plan for 200,000 tpa LFP cathode material (Rs 4,800 cr over ~5-6 years).
Birla Tyres acquired out of insolvency with Dalmia Bharat Refractories (NCLT order 19-Oct-2023); plant restarted May-2025.

1.08 cr warrants at Rs 316 issued to promoters and identified investors (Rs 342 cr in total); converted Aug-Nov 2025, the promoters' 1 cr warrants on 7-Nov-2025 (Rs 237 cr balance paid), lifting the promoter stake to 52.5%.

70,000 tpa speciality carbon black line (Rs 220 cr; commercial production Feb-2026) takes speciality capacity to 130,000 tpa; coal tar distillation debottlenecked to 600,000 tpa; liquid pitch terminals at Haldia and Mangalore; investments in Sicona (May-2025), IBC (16.24%, later 19.44%) and Invati (40%).
200 tpa anode material plant commissioned at Mahistikry (23-Apr-2026), entirely in-house technology.
Q1FY27 record quarter; CNT (200 tpa, Rs 70 cr) and SSCB (6,000 tpa, Rs 170 cr) projects announced; ICRA upgraded the long-term rating to AA (Stable).
Board approved a scheme to demerge DBRL's tyre business into HSCL (1 HSCL share per 260 DBRL shares).

corporateActions.fact: 50,45,74,175 shares at 21-Sep-2026 (49.37 cr at Mar-2025): +1.08 cr warrant shares in FY26 and ESOP allotments. Face value Rs 1.
Final dividend Rs 0.80 per share for FY26 (about 5% of EPS).
Himadri Employee Stock Option Plan 2016; 53,896 options outstanding and exercisable at Sep-2026; a new ESOP 2026 plan was put to the 2026 AGM.
Repeated Rs 100-200 cr commercial paper issues through FY26, all repaid on time; bank lines used and parked in deposits for a spread (management).

governance.board: 7 directors: 3 promoter executives (father and two sons) and 4 independent directors (Girish Vanvari, Gopal Malpani, Rita Bhattacharya, Amitabh Srivastava from Apr-2025). The CMD is also chairman.
governance.auditor: Singhi & Co, Kolkata (appointed 2022 for five years); unqualified opinion on FY26 accounts
governance.relatedParty: Himadri holds 12.49 lakh optionally convertible preference shares of Modern Hi-Rise, its own promoter holding company, carried at Rs 182.6 cr (allotted Mar-2019 under an amalgamation with appointed date 1-Jun-2018; 1% non-cumulative; convertible into 7.7% of Modern Hi-Rise or redeemable at the issuer's option within 20 years), plus small stakes in group companies Himadri Credit & Finance and Himadri e-Carbon. The tyre business is funded through Dalmia Bharat Refractories NCDs held by Himadri: Rs 486.5 cr at Mar-26 (Rs 187.2 cr at Mar-25), plus 8% DBRL preference shares; a demerger scheme now brings the tyre business into HSCL.
governance.credit: ICRA long-term AA (Stable), upgraded from AA- (Positive) on 10-Jul-2026; short-term A1+; Rs 2,480.86 cr rated

accounting.fact: The company's EBITDA (Rs 1,006 cr in FY26) excludes forex; the P&L books forex in other expenses (FY26 loss Rs 43.6 cr, Q1FY27 loss Rs 25.2 cr). Screener's EBITDA (Rs 962 cr) is after the loss.

Rs 171 cr in FY26 (Rs 52 cr FY25; Rs 56 cr in Q1FY27): interest on deposits partly funded by short-term borrowing (borrowings rose from Rs 313 cr to Rs 770 cr in FY26), mutual-fund gains and fair-value gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres instruments. It was 17% of FY26 pre-tax profit.

Of FY26 other income of Rs 171.3 cr, Rs 100.0 cr was a fair-value gain on non-current investments carried at fair value through P&L (IBC, Sicona and similar; Rs 0.2 cr in FY25); interest on bank deposits was Rs 43.5 cr. Excluding the fair-value gain, FY26 pre-tax profit would have been ~10% lower.

Company net cash Rs 121 cr at Mar-26 (Q4 call; the Jul-2026 deck shows Rs 113 cr), down from ~Rs 371-392 cr at Mar-25 despite record profit, as capex, strategic investments and working capital absorbed cash.
Screener: cash from operations Rs 382 cr in FY26 vs EBITDA Rs 962 cr (40%); inventory days rose from 68 to 96.

Invati (40%) and Himadri Birla Tyre Manufacturer (49%) are consolidated as subsidiaries on contractual control (Ind AS 110), so tyre revenue is consolidated while the tyre plant sits in DBRL until the demerger.
